header: THE DSP TAB OF THE STEEL CARD (pure, no React): it shows what the Durgapur Steel Plant makes to sell, and what the same kind of steel costs in the Durgapur market. TWO KINDS OF FIGURE, KEPT APART:

* PRODUCTS: what each mill rolls, its sizes and its capacity, given exactly as the plant's own "Operation Department Manual" (the DSP JO Manual 2022, revised plant-specific manual) states them, with the page.

* QUOTES: the Durgapur rates a private trade-price site (Ayron Mart, ayronmart.com) publishes every day, read on 15 Nov 2026 from its tables dated 13 Nov 2026 (rupees per tonne, GST NOT included: the site says 18% GST is extra). A quote is the market's rate for that KIND of steel in Durgapur. It is NOT DSP's or SAIL's selling price: SAIL sells at its own list and dealer rates, which nobody publishes, and a market quote is for a given size (TMT 12 mm, while DSP rolls 20 and 25 mm) and is mostly the re-rollers' price. The card says so. I estimate nothing: a product with no quote has none, and the card says why.

* PRODUCTION: what DSP produced, as SAIL's own annual reports (FY 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26) and its FY26 results presentation state it, each with the PDF page and the words it was read from. The reports give DSP's hot metal, crude steel, saleable steel and finished steel by year for some years and the output of three units (the Bloom cum Round Caster, the Medium Structural Mill and the Merchant Mill) for 2024-25 only; for 2025-26 they say only "highest ever finished steel" and give the product mix in per cent. I leave out what they do not state (TMT, structurals, blooms, billets, wheels and axles in tonnes, month by month), and the card says so. The reports give some figures in lakh tonnes: I divide them by 10 into million tonnes (MT). A figure worked out from two stated figures is marked "worked out".

I fetch nothing while the card is open: this is a reviewed file with its sources and dates, like mos.ts. When you refresh it, change the quotes, `asOf` and `readOn` together; the card warns when the quotes are old.

behaviours: six quotes, each with a source page on ayronmart.com and the line it was read from
each quote's rupees are the number in its line, and its date is the date in its line (13-November-2026)
the day's change is the one in the line: ▲ is positive, ▼ negative, (X) none
no quote is a GST-inclusive figure: the site says 18% GST is extra, and the card says so beside every price
the second billet report is a different site and is close to the first (within 3%), as a check, not a replacement
age: 2 days on 15 Nov, 0 on the day, 7 on 20 Nov (the last day before the warning), 8 on 21 Nov
the warning comes after seven days
dates are written 13 Nov 2026
sixteen cities, each once; Durgapur's figure is the TMT quote
Durgapur is the cheapest of the sixteen; Goa the dearest, 15.7% above (52,300 against 45,200)
the list is in order from the cheapest
seven products with distinct ids, each with its mill, sizes, capacity and a manual page
every quote a product names exists, and every quote belongs to a product
joists and beams, and wheels and axles, have no quote and say why; no price is made up for them
a product with a quote says the quote is not its own price (a different size, a market rate, or not DSP's)
the plant's capacity is hot metal 2.40, crude steel 2.20, saleable steel 2.12 MT, in that order of size
wheel and axle capacity adds up as the manual says: 28,000 + 4,500 = 32,500 tonnes
two by-products listed, with no quote and a manual page
four financial years, 2022-23 to 2025-26, in order, each with a source that is a sail.co.in document with a PDF page and the words it was read from
each stated figure is in the words it was read from (2.56/2.29/2.18 as the previous best, 2.57/2.30/2.21, 2.50/2.26/2.15 and 1.126)
the figures of each year are as stated: 2022-23 2.56/2.29/2.18; 2023-24 2.57/2.30/2.21; 2024-25 2.50/2.26/2.15 and finished 1.126; 2025-26 has no tonnes
each year's figures are in order of size as steel is made: hot metal above crude steel above saleable steel above finished steel
the 2025-26 product mix is 54.7% longs and 45.3% semis, adding to 100, and is read from SAIL's presentation page 14
the three units of 2024-25 are the report's lakh tonnes divided by 10: BRC 6.26 -> 0.626, MSM 5.57 -> 0.557, MM 4.28 -> 0.428 MT, and the words say so
the two finishing units are within finished steel (0.557 + 0.428 = 0.985 < 1.126)
worked out for 2024-25: semi-finished 1.024 MT (2.15 less 1.126), finished 52.4% of saleable steel, 0.141 MT of finished steel beyond the two mills
the finished share has risen: 52.4% in 2024-25 (worked out), longs 54.7% in 2025-26 (stated)
change on the year: crude steel +0.4% (2.30 on 2.29), -1.7% (2.26 on 2.30); saleable -2.7% (2.15 on 2.21); nothing when a year has no figure or the earlier is zero
wheel, tyre and axle items to Indian Railways: 42,024, 45,656 and 47,200 (+8.6% and +3.4%), 1,689 Vande Bharat wheels in 2025-26, each number in its source's words
every product says what is published about its production and what is not (a 'Produced' line), and none claims tonnes the reports do not give
ten financial years, 2016-17 to 2025-26, in order, one each
four years have a figure (2018-19 2.52, 2022-23 2.56, 2023-24 2.57, 2024-25 2.50); the six others are empty, not estimated
each stated year has a source (a sail.co.in document, a PDF page, the words) and the number is in those words
each empty year says why in words (no DSP figure stated; or the ceiling the reports do give), never a number

the earlier years are bounded by what the reports say: 2016-17 and 2017-18 below 2.52 (2018-19 was the best ever), 2019-20 to 2021-22 not above 2.52 (the 2022-23 report names 2.52 as the best before 2022-23)
the series agrees with the yearly table: 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 hot metal are the same figures
the 2022-23 conflict is admitted: the 2022-23 report's own 2.57 is quoted beside the 2.56 that the 2023-24 report gives, and the choice is explained
no stated year is above the best of 2.57 MT, and the best is 2023-24; hot metal is in MT with no 'lakh'
the capacity note names the other sources: 2.45 MT in a Lok Sabha reply and the CAG's audit
no 'lakh' and no 'Mt' in the DSP figures (million tonnes are written MT)
